tx-tarrant-2026-district-clerk-smith-nat.name: Nathan Smith
tx-tarrant-2026-district-clerk-smith-nat.bio: Army veteran and Bronze Star recipient; former staffer for a Tarrant County Commissioner.

positions.stance: Will assign District Clerk staff to Central Magistration from day one, present 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.
Will work to return the jury summons process to the District Clerk under Texas law and prioritize prompt notification of trial cancellations.
Will audit the records fee schedule, bring it into full compliance with state law, and treat expanding public access to court documents as an obligation.
Will commission an independent assessment of the court software system and present the findings openly to commissioners and the public.
Will publish regular, plain-language performance data so the public can see how the courts are functioning.

tx-tarrant-2026-county-clerk-nicholson-m.name: Mary Louise Nicholson
tx-tarrant-2026-county-clerk-nicholson-m.bio: Tarrant County Clerk since 2011; previously served eight years on the Tarrant County Sheriff's command staff.

positions.stance: Wants to simplify access to records "as much as the law and technology permits" while preserving historical records.
Describes herself as a fiscally conservative Republican who has operated the office under budget, using technology to save taxpayer dollars.
Determined to protect residents from records fraud, including photo ID for land-record filings and a free Property Fraud Alert service.
Treats customer service as a signature issue, with the mission "to provide cost-effective services and a satisfying citizen experience."

tx-tarrant-2026-county-clerk-bean-lydia.name: Lydia Bean
tx-tarrant-2026-county-clerk-bean-lydia.bio: Founder and President of Equipa, a consulting firm advising non-profits and foundations; co-founder of Whistleblower Aid.

positions.stance: Says the County Clerk's office needs "fresh leadership, accountability, and accessibility."
Says Tarrant County needs a County Clerk "who will protect free and fair elections and stand up to extremism."

tx-williamson-2026-county-clerk-fairbrot.name: Bill Fairbrother
tx-williamson-2026-county-clerk-fairbrot.bio: Chief Deputy County Clerk of Williamson County.

positions.stance: Committed to a smooth transition, working closely with office staff to keep daily operations consistent.
Primary objective is accurate, prompt, and correct handling of vital records, Court at Law records, and Commissioners Court records.

tx-williamson-2026-county-clerk-block-er.name: Erin Block
tx-williamson-2026-county-clerk-block-er.bio: Accountant with experience in manufacturing, general contracting, nonprofit management, and government finance.

positions.stance: Will modernize county systems so government keeps up with growth and works smoothly when people need it most.
Believes residents deserve clear expectations and reliable timelines on how long things take and where their request stands.
Believes county government should serve people with kindness so every resident feels supported, respected, and never lost in the process.

tx-williamson-2026-treasurer-callahan-ca.name: Carole Callahan
tx-williamson-2026-treasurer-callahan-ca.bio: Assistant Treasurer of Williamson County for eight years; former Georgetown ISD math teacher and congressional executive assistant.

tx-williamson-2026-tax-assessor-unexp-to.name: Catherine Totty
tx-williamson-2026-tax-assessor-unexp-to.bio: Appointed Williamson County Tax Assessor-Collector in 2026, with more than 25 years in banking, finance, customer service, and operations.

positions.stance: Committed to friendly, responsive, and dependable service focused on enhancing tax office services for residents.
Emphasizes protecting taxpayer resources through efficient operations, sound financial management, and accountable leadership.
Emphasizes modernizing processes and adopting technology so residents receive faster, more convenient county services.

tx-williamson-2026-tax-assessor-unexp-ha.name: Eric Hanke
tx-williamson-2026-tax-assessor-unexp-ha.bio: Financial educator with the Texas County and District Retirement System for 12 years.

positions.stance: Will prioritize educating residents on how taxes and property tax rates are set so they know their rights as taxpayers.
Will maintain high customer service while improving workflow and efficiency to meet the needs of a growing county.
Will collect and distribute taxes "with the utmost care and accountability" so schools and first responders have needed resources.
Will use technology to modernize tax office processes, save taxpayer resources, and minimize customer wait times.

fl-pinellas-2026-bocc-d2-scott-brian.name: Brian Scott
fl-pinellas-2026-bocc-d2-scott-brian.bio: President of Escot Bus Lines; Pinellas County Commissioner for District 2 and 2025 Commission Chairman.

positions.stance: Believes government must live within its means, with responsible budgeting that protects taxpayers and eliminates wasteful spending.
Believes local government must adjust tax rates to prevent "backdoor tax increases on homeowners"; supports lowering the millage rate.
Supports investing in stormwater systems, flood protection, and emergency preparedness so the county can recover quickly after storms.
Supports continued beach renourishment and coastal protection projects to safeguard the shoreline.

fl-pinellas-2026-bocc-d2-hughes-tim.name: Tim Hughes
fl-pinellas-2026-bocc-d2-hughes-tim.bio: Twenty years in the Watershed Management Branch of a public works department; Conservation Chairman of the Suncoast Sierra Club.

positions.stance: Supports safe, affordable housing, including converting aging mobile home parks into resilient, energy-efficient condominium communities.
Will establish an inter-governmental resiliency task force and SMART flood-reduction plans aimed at lowering property and flood insurance premiums.
Supports restoring tree canopies, expanding urban greenspaces, and protecting natural land as infrastructure against climate impacts and heat.
Supports upgrading aging stormwater, wastewater, and drinking water systems to prevent flooding and protect public health.
Supports cutting red tape for rooftop and community solar to lower utility bills and promote renewable energy.

ny-suffolk-2026-county-comptroller-losqu.name: Daniel P Losquadro
ny-suffolk-2026-county-comptroller-losqu.bio: Brookhaven Town Highway Superintendent since 2013; former Suffolk County Legislator and New York State Assemblyman.

il-dupage-2026-sheriff-coolidge-peter.name: Peter Joseph Coolidge
il-dupage-2026-sheriff-coolidge-peter.bio: Spent 28 years with the DuPage County Sheriff's Office in corrections, law enforcement, and courthouse administration.

positions.stance: Prioritizes "true transparency that builds trust," so people know how the sheriff's department makes decisions.
Will improve public safety outcomes by giving deputies the right tools, staffing, and training.
Supports a return to "true community policing" to make the Sheriff's Office a consistent, positive presence in every neighborhood.
Committed to running the jail "with absolute integrity," ensuring community security and full protection of rights under the law.

il-dupage-2026-treasurer-yoo-yeena.name: Yeena Yoo
il-dupage-2026-treasurer-yoo-yeena.bio: Attorney and DuPage County Board member representing District 2.

positions.stance: Will strengthen financial practices and update processes so county government delivers exceptional service.
Will work with county IT and the software vendor to resolve tax system problems and address duplicate tax payments.
Will redesign the Treasurer's website and improve the online payment portal to make property tax information clearer and easier to use.
Will take the office into communities and use digital outreach so eligible residents learn about property tax relief programs.

il-dupage-2026-treasurer-henry-gwen.name: Gwen Henry
il-dupage-2026-treasurer-henry-gwen.bio: DuPage County Treasurer/Collector since 2009; certified public accountant and former Mayor of Wheaton.

positions.stance: Safeguard taxpayer funds through careful budgeting, responsible investment practices, and strong financial oversight.
Works to make county financial information more accessible and understandable for residents.

il-dupage-2026-forest-preserve-president.name: Daniel Hebreard
il-dupage-2026-forest-preserve-president.bio: President of the Forest Preserve District of DuPage County since 2018; previously a District ranger for 13 years.

positions.stance: Says his mission is "to be a guardian of our taxpayers' money."
Says his mission is to be "an enthusiastic steward of our incredible natural resources."
Says his mission is to make sure all preserve spaces "provide a safe environment for our millions of visitors."
Protect and restore land the District already owns using best scientific practices, and selectively purchase land aligned with the preserve purpose.
"Stop the spending spree"; supports on-budget, on-time projects and reducing District debt to lower property taxes.
Supports safe access, education, and recreation for all residents, including "Pop-up Preserves" in communities without them.
